unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled Ohio sections define 'legislative agent' by qualitative time/purpose standards and require registration within 10 days of engagement, but they do not set any dollar-based compensation threshold for when registration is required.

The bundled Ohio sections require registration based on 'engagement' as a legislative agent/executive agency lobbyist/retirement system lobbyist, not on an expenditures dollar threshold; no dollar trigger for registration appears in the provided text.

The definition of 'legislative agent' refers to being engaged 'during at least a portion of the individual's time' and 'as one of the individual's main purposes' (and other lobbyist definitions use 'regular and substantial basis'), but no numeric time-percent threshold is specified in the provided text.

The bundled statute sets a $50 cumulative itemization trigger specifically for meals/food and beverages, but it does not state any overall de minimis dollar threshold below which lobbying expenditures generally need not be reported.

The bundled statute does not provide any numeric time-percent de minimis threshold governing whether lobbying activity or expenditures must be reported; it sets reporting periods and itemization rules but no such percentage trigger.
